en: The Questions of Milinda,
Great Chapter 10:
The Question on Faith Characterized by Serene Confidence (Sampasādana-lakkhaṇa-saddhā-pañha)
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of faith?
"Faith, Great King, has the characteristic of serene confidence and the characteristic of leaping forward," he replied.
“Venerable sir, how does faith have the characteristic of clarification?
“Great king, when faith arises, it suppresses the hindrances; the mind becomes free from hindrances, clear, serene, and undisturbed.
It is in this way, great king, that faith has the characteristic of clarification.”
“Make a simile,” [the king said].
“It is just as if, great king, a wheel-turning monarch, having set out on a journey together with a fourfold army, were to cross a small body of water;
that water would be agitated by elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry.”
It would become turbid, stirred up, and muddy.
And when the Wheel-turning Monarch had emerged, he might command his men, “Ho! Bring water, I shall drink. Now, suppose there were a water-clearing gem belonging to the king.
Saying, “So be it, Your Majesty,” those men, having assented to the Wheel-turning Monarch, [would take] that water-clearing gem...

Suppose they were to throw a jewel into the water; as soon as that jewel is thrown into the water, the shells, seaweed, and moss would disappear, the mud would settle, and the water would become clear, serene, and undisturbed.
Then they would offer the drinking water to the Wheel-turning Monarch, saying, "Drink, O Lord, drink the water."

"Great King, just as water is, so should the mind be regarded; just as those men are, so should the practitioner be regarded; just as the shells, seaweed, moss, and mud are, so should the defilements be regarded.
Just as the water-clearing gem is, so should faith be regarded.
Just as when the water-clearing gem is merely placed in the water, the shells, seaweed, and moss disappear and the mud settles, so that the water becomes clear."
“Just as water is clear and undisturbed, even so, Great King, when faith arises, it suppresses the hindrances; the mind becomes free from hindrances—transparent, serene, and undisturbed.
Thus, Great King, faith has the characteristic of clarity.”
“Beautiful, venerable Nāgasena!
Thus ends the tenth question, on faith characterized by serene confidence.
